31 The diagram shows a metal block.

The block has sides of length a, b and c as shown, and its volume is V. Each charge carrier has a
charge –q and the number density of the charge carriers in the metal is n. It takes each charge
carrier an average time of t to pass through the block.
What is an expression for the current I ?
A
I = nqabc
B
I = nqV
t
C
I = nqbc
t
D
I = nqaV

hints: Notice the number density $n$ and the block volume $V$ - combine them to find the total number of charge carriers $nV$ in the block.
Recall that current $I$ is rate of flow of charge, $I = Q/t$, where $Q$ is the magnitude of charge passing in time $t$.
Use the statement that each carrier takes average time $t$ to pass through the block to link the total charge $nqV$ to the current $I$.
walkthrough: Find the total number of free carriers in the block from number density times volume: $N = nV$.
Each carrier has charge of magnitude $q$, ignoring the minus sign for magnitude of current, so total mobile charge in the block is $Q = Nq = nqV$.
Current is defined as $I = Q/t$ for charge passing a point in time $t$.
The time for the carriers initially in the block to drift through and past a cross-section is the given transit time $t$.
Substitute $Q$: $I = nqV/t$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This gives total charge $nqV$ since $abc=V$, but current is charge per unit time so division by $t$ is missing.

B.explanation: Total charge of magnitude $nqV$ in the block passes through in average time $t$, so $I = nqV/t$.

C.explanation: The product $bc$ is an area, not the volume $V=abc$, so $nqbc/t$ counts only part of the carriers in the block.

D.explanation: Multiplying by both $a$ and $V$ double-counts volume and omits division by $t$, giving units of $\text{C m}^{4}$ rather than $\text{A}$.
